cost_basis.cheapest_design: The plain version, which is also the starting design: S2 labels every interviewee turn in two calls (tuning interviews, held-out interviews; about $0.08 per pass) and S3 drafts every row in one call (about $0.014), and no second model in S2 or S3. Per-interview calls (about $0.15 on the tuning interviews), per-turn calls (about $0.40 on the tuning interviews) and per-proposition drafts (at most 6 calls) are stages added only if the plain version shows a gap on the tuning interviews or on the number and passage check; per-turn calls are not the cheapest design. The four language-model controls (about $0.16 once per corpus with the plain version) are kept because the brief requires them. The dummy, word-list count and TF-IDF regression run locally at no model cost; the fresh reviewer is a Claude Code session on the subscription; S1, S5 and S7 call no model. Quality decides, not cost.

plain_baseline.answer_path: S2's measured labels per interviewee turn (shown in the Measurement tab) and S3's verdicts and meta-inferences (shown in the Joint display tab)
cases: Open Science S2: the plain version (the instrument and every interviewee turn of one split in one call, two calls) is the starting design, scored on the tuning interviews against the word-list count and the author's coding
Open Science S3: the plain version (one call over all six propositions with the mapping and the measured result) is the starting design, checked by the number and passage check
plain_baseline.when: S2's tuning-interview run and S3's first run; a stage below is built only if that run shows a gap, and is then compared with the plain version on the same tuning interviews or propositions

stage_effects.stage: S2 one call per interview, instead of the plain version's one call per split
stage_effects.gap: a call over half the corpus can leave turns unlabelled, copy a neighbour's label, or agree with the author's coding less than the word-list count does

stage_effects.stage: S2 one call per interviewee turn, instead of one call per interview
stage_effects.gap: labels from one long call can influence one another and long-context labelling can lose accuracy

stage_effects.stage: S3 one draft per mapped proposition, instead of the plain version's one call over all propositions
stage_effects.gap: one call over all propositions can cite a number not in the measured result, give a verdict the mapping refuses, or blur which proposition a figure speaks to
